rationale: ANNOTATION TYPE REFERENCES (M14 owner ruling 2026-10-18: 'annotations produce ZERO relationship rows - a real missing relationship'). An annotation is a TYPE mention (JLS 9.6 declares an annotation interface, JLS 9.7 uses it), so every annotation site owes a `references` edge to the annotation type under the label the analyzer already uses for every other type mention. The pinned grammar has TWO node types for one construct (`marker_annotation` = `@Override`, `annotation` = `@SuppressWarnings("x")`, differing only by the argument list) and pre-fix BOTH emitted nothing to the relationship channel - the names reached `decorators`/`metadata.annotations` as payload only. Measured pre-fix on this exact fixture: 0 rows carrying `isAnnotation`. The Lead's census over a 203-file corpus draw: 1,475 `marker_annotation` + 119 `annotation` nodes, 0 relationship rows. Authored from Java semantics before observing the fix: every position Java permits an annotation in is pinned here (class, method, field single, field MULTI-DECLARATOR per JLS 8.3 one annotation annotates both variables, type-use JLS 9.7.4, formal parameter, local variable, enum constant, record component), plus the two spellings (bare leaf and fully qualified) and the repeated-annotation pair. Every expectation carries confidenceMin 0.95 because the spelling is written in the declaration, not inferred. THE FORBIDS are the four ways this emission can silently lie: a qualified annotation truncated to its leaf (a second spelling of one name), an annotation treated as an `import`, the `@` sigil kept in the target, and a parameter/local/record-component annotation attributed to a span that publishes no symbol (the annotation must be carried by the enclosing declaration, the same attribution the lane already uses for those positions' declared_type references).
